title: Best Athletic Shorts for Men 2026: 5 Pairs Ranked
description: From $30 Under Armour to $68 Lululemon — the 5 best men's athletic shorts of 2026 ranked by liner quality, chafe resistance, and mobility.
lede: The difference between great athletic shorts and forgettable ones becomes obvious in the first mile of a run or the first set of squats. Poor liner construction causes chafing that accumulates across a workout. Inseam length affects stride mechanics. Fabric weight determines comfort in heat. These five were selected because each is genuinely strong in at least one of those areas — not just well-branded.
methodology: Each pair is compared on liner construction and the chafe complaints runners raise in owner reviews, inseam length accuracy, pocket security during dynamic movement, fabric breathability in 70°F+ conditions, and construction durability after 15+ wash cycles.

sections.heading: How to Choose Athletic Shorts
paragraphs: Inseam length is personal and matters more than most buyers account for. The 5-inch inseam is the standard athletic cut — it allows full range of motion without being restrictive. The 7-inch and 9-inch cuts are more modest but can limit stride. Knowing your preferred length before buying prevents the most common return.

subsections.heading: Liner vs. No Liner
paragraphs: Built-in liner shorts eliminate the need for separate compression shorts but the quality of the liner determines whether they're an asset or a liability. A loose, poorly-attached liner shifts during movement and causes friction. A well-constructed liner (Lululemon Pace Breaker, Nike Challenger) stays in place and feels like nothing is there. Liner-free shorts give you full control over compression choice but require a separate layer.

subsections.heading: Inseam Length and Activity
paragraphs: 5-inch: standard for running, HIIT, and most gym work — allows full range of motion. 7-inch: more moderate cut that works across most activities without looking purely athletic. 9-inch: conservative cut for strength training, yoga, or those who prefer more coverage. Most of the picks in this list are 5-inch because that's where athletic performance is strongest.

subsections.heading: Pocket Design for Workouts
paragraphs: Phone pockets in running shorts deserve specific scrutiny. A phone pocket that allows the phone to bounce during running is worse than no pocket at all. Zippered side pockets or the rear zippered pocket common on running shorts (Nike Challenger has this) prevent both bouncing and accidental loss during dynamic movement.

subsections.heading: Fabric Weight and Ventilation
paragraphs: Ultra-lightweight fabrics (Gymshark Vital, Nike Challenger) shed heat faster during cardio and feel less clingy when damp with sweat. Mid-weight fabrics (Under Armour Launch) feel slightly more substantial but may trap more heat. For outdoor summer running, lighter is almost always better. For gym strength work where temperature regulation is less of an issue, weight matters less.

sections.heading: Bottom line
paragraphs: The Lululemon Pace Breaker 5" is the best liner short available without qualification — the liner engineering is genuinely the best in category. Nike Dri-FIT Challenger is the smart everyday pick at $35 — solid performance with a rear zip pocket that the premium options often skip. Ten Thousand Versatility Short is worth the premium for anyone who wants one pair of shorts that works across every athletic context, from running to lifting to swimming.

faqs.q: What length athletic shorts should I get?
faqs.a: 5-inch inseam is the most versatile for athletic performance — it provides full range of motion for running, cycling, and gym work. If you prefer more modest coverage or primarily do strength training, 7-inch is a comfortable middle ground. 9-inch shorts are the most conservative and work best for yoga or those who simply prefer more leg coverage. When in doubt for performance, go shorter.

faqs.q: Are built-in liner shorts better than separate compression shorts?
faqs.a: For convenience, yes — one garment is faster to put on and reduces laundry. But quality varies significantly. High-quality liner shorts (Lululemon Pace Breaker) use pouch construction and attached liners that genuinely stay in place. Lower-quality liner shorts have loose liners that shift during movement and cause chafing. If you've had bad experiences with built-in liners, it's likely the brand rather than the format — quality liner construction is genuinely effective.

faqs.q: How often should you replace athletic shorts?
faqs.a: With regular washing (3–4 times per week), athletic shorts typically last 1–2 years before the elastic waistband loses tension and the fabric loses shape. Signs it's time to replace: the waistband rolls or feels loose during activity, the fabric has permanent stretch-out in the seat or thighs, or the liner (if present) has begun separating at the seams.

faqs.q: Can athletic shorts be worn casually?
faqs.a: 5-inch athletic shorts with clean, minimal branding (Ten Thousand, Gymshark Vital) read more versatile than obvious running shorts. Pair with a clean t-shirt or casual button-down and clean sneakers for casual settings. Very short inseams and visible liner construction read as workout-specific regardless of pairing. For shorts that genuinely work athletically and casually, Gymshark Vital and Ten Thousand are the strongest options in this list.

faqs.q: What's the best material for athletic shorts?
faqs.a: Polyester-elastane blends (typically 87% polyester / 13% elastane) are the best performers: they wick sweat, stretch fully without restriction, and dry quickly. 100% polyester without elastane is less flexible — acceptable for lighter activity but limiting during full range-of-motion movements. Avoid cotton for intense athletic use — it absorbs sweat rather than wicking it, becoming heavy and slow to dry.

products.review: The Lululemon Pace Breaker 5" ($68) is the standard by which other liner shorts are judged. The liner is engineered with a pouch construction that stays anchored regardless of movement intensity — no shifting, no chafing, no awareness that a liner exists. The Swift Ultra fabric is genuinely weightless and breathable at a level that's physically noticeable during cardio. At $68 it's the most expensive pair here, but the liner engineering justifies the price for serious runners.
pros: Liner engineering is the best in category — stays in place
Swift Ultra fabric feels weightless during cardio
cons: $68 is the premium end of athletic shorts pricing
No rear zip pocket — a meaningful omission for runners

products.review: Ten Thousand Versatility Short ($68) is designed to eliminate the need for separate workout shorts and casual shorts. Quick-dry nylon, clean minimal branding, a functional liner option (available separately), and a cut that doesn't scream athletic. For anyone who wants one pair of shorts that works running, lifting, swimming, and going out casually, Ten Thousand solved the problem better than anyone else at this price point.
pros: Clean minimal branding allows athletic-to-casual styling
Quick-dry nylon works for swimming and running equally
Versatile enough to replace multiple specialized shorts
cons: Liner is a separate purchase — adds to total cost
Less specialized for pure running performance than Pace Breaker

products.review: Nike Dri-FIT Challenger 5" ($35) is the smart value play: solid athletic construction at half the Lululemon price. Dri-FIT wicking is genuine — Nike's moisture management in this fabric is noticeably better than budget competition. The rear zip pocket is a feature Lululemon inexplicably omits on the Pace Breaker, and it makes the Challenger more functional for runners who carry a key or card. The liner quality is below Pace Breaker but serviceable for most users.
pros: Rear zip pocket is practical for runners — missing from many competitors
Dri-FIT wicking is effective and well-proven
Half the price of Lululemon for 80% of the performance
cons: Liner quality is below Lululemon for dedicated runners
Nike branding is more visible than minimal-look alternatives

products.review: Gymshark Vital Shorts ($45) nail the aesthetic that Nike and Under Armour can't quite achieve — they look like something you'd wear casually but perform like actual athletic shorts. The fabric is lightweight and quick-drying, the fit is tailored without being restrictive, and the branding is minimal. For gym training and daily wear, the Vital is strong at $45. Running performance is solid but not as focused as the Pace Breaker.
pros: Tailored fit looks intentional rather than athletic
Minimal branding works for casual-to-gym use
Lightweight fabric performs well for HIIT and strength training
cons: Not specifically engineered for running liner performance
Limited pocket functionality compared to Nike Challenger

products.review: Under Armour Launch 5" ($30) is the most affordable pair in this comparison and delivers reliable athletic function at that price point. UA HeatGear fabric wicks effectively in high-temperature conditions and the construction holds up to regular washing. The liner quality is consistent with other UA products — functional without being exceptional. A solid everyday training short at a price where wear-and-replace every year is financially painless.
pros: HeatGear fabric wicks effectively in warm conditions
Reliable construction consistent with Under Armour's track record
cons: Liner quality is basic compared to Lululemon or Nike
Fit runs slightly large — sizing down is sometimes necessary
